# Emmanuel Effiom Duke

> Personal site of Emmanuel Effiom Duke (also Emmanuel Duke): AI builder, mechanical engineer, technology entrepreneur and researcher based in Enugu State, Nigeria. Founder of Dukers LTD. B.Eng. Mechanical Engineering, University of Nigeria, Nsukka.

Canonical pages: https://duker.me/ (overview) and https://duker.me/about/ (full biography). All content is plain HTML.

## Sections

- [Ventures](https://duker.me/#ventures): Dukers LTD (founder, https://dukersltd.com), Teger AI (https://tegerai.tech), Transly (https://transly.software)
- [Projects](https://duker.me/#projects): AI-safety research code, fintech (AxiosPay), agriculture, geospatial and security projects
- [About](https://duker.me/about/): full biography
- [Experience](https://duker.me/#experience): roles and dates
- [Research](https://duker.me/#publications): research interests and publications
- [Writing](https://duker.me/articles/): articles and technical notes
- [Community](https://duker.me/#leadership): mentoring and leadership
- [Contact](https://duker.me/#contact): emmanuel.duke@dukersltd.com

## Articles

<!--ARTICLES:START-->
- [Building a Metaculus forecasting bot](https://duker.me/articles/metaculus-forecasting-bot/): Lessons from an LLM forecasting bot in Metaculus AI tournaments: silent research failures, extremized toss-ups, and replacing vibes-tuning with measurement.
- [Ask the calendar, not the model](https://duker.me/articles/llm-knowledge-cutoff-probe/): Measuring nine language models' real knowledge cutoffs with dated-event bisection: every model that self-reported a cutoff was wrong, some by over a year.
- [Designing Teger AI to explain phishing](https://duker.me/articles/designing-teger-ai/): How Teger AI, an explainable social-engineering defence for Gmail and Slack, pairs deterministic signals with AI analysis and treats every message as untrusted.
- [Four false positives and one real signal](https://duker.me/articles/secret-loyalties-audit/): A weights-first audit of three model organisms for secret loyalties at the Apart Research hackathon, and the workflow that rejected four false positives.
- [SPD meets a real grokked transformer](https://duker.me/articles/spd-real-transformer/): Applying Stochastic Parameter Decomposition to a transformer that grokked modular addition: the ground truth was verified, but the components never specialized.
- [Clustering SPD components into mechanisms](https://duker.me/articles/spd-mechanism-clustering/): A CPU pilot showing SPD subcomponents can be grouped into ground-truth mechanisms automatically, and why specialization is the real bottleneck.
- [Do models represent deception alike?](https://duker.me/articles/deception-feature-universality/): Do different architectures learn similar internal representations of deception cues? A toy-scale test, and why the first null was too weak to answer.
- [The reward spread; the warning didn't](https://duker.me/articles/reward-generalization-early-warning/): Reproducing unintended reward generalization in an inspectable toy model, and a negative result: internal signals gave no early warning.
<!--ARTICLES:END-->
